## Load packages

WGCNA is attached because it looks up its correlation function (`bicor`) by name; it masks
`stats::cor()` with a compatible version.

```{r setup}
pacman::p_load(here, WGCNA, limma, dplyr, tibble, tidyr, purrr, ggplot2, readxl, writexl)
here::i_am("04_Network/01_modules/a_script/01_modules.qmd")
disableWGCNAThreads()
```

## Read inputs

The question: which proteins move together across samples, whether or not a curated set groups
them, and do those groups respond to training, differ between the arms, or track muscle growth?
WGCNA (weighted gene co-expression network analysis; Langfelder and Horvath 2008,
doi:10.1186/1471-2105-9-559) groups proteins into modules by correlation and summarises each
module by its eigengene, the first principal component of its members.

Inputs: the protein estimates, the stage 02 design and contrasts, the association designs from
`03_Protein_Association`, and the gene sets and protein-to-gene map from `00_build_gene_sets`.

```{r read}
stage <- here("04_Network", "01_modules")
proteins <- readRDS(here("01_Preprocess", "02_Quantification", "c_data", "proteins.rds"))
d <- readRDS(here("02_Differential_Expression", "01_Design", "c_data", "design.rds"))
association_designs <- readRDS(here(
  "02_Differential_Expression", "03_Protein_Association", "c_data", "association_designs.rds"
))
sets_dir <- here("03_Pathway_Enrichment", "00_build_gene_sets", "c_data")
sets <- readRDS(file.path(sets_dir, "gene_sets.rds"))
gene_of <- read_excel(file.path(sets_dir, "00_build_gene_sets.xlsx"), "protein_gene_map") |>
  filter(selected)
targets <- proteins$targets
stopifnot(identical(colnames(proteins$E), rownames(d$design)))
dim(proteins$E)
```

## Remove participant

Participant explains most of the leading variation, so a network on raw abundance would mostly
group proteins by who the biopsy came from. The WGCNA FAQ asks for such effects to be removed
first, and the Bioconductor forum answer for paired designs (support.bioconductor.org/p/86486,
/p/126464) is `removeBatchEffect()` with participant as the batch and the treatment-by-time group
as the design to protect. Every protein enters: the FAQ advises against filtering by differential
expression.

```{r adjust}
adjusted <- removeBatchEffect(
  proteins$E, batch = targets$participant, design = model.matrix(~ 0 + group, targets)
)
expression <- t(adjusted)
```

## Pick the soft threshold

A signed network keeps the sign of correlation, so proteins that move in opposite directions do
not join. Biweight midcorrelation (bicor) down-weights outlying samples; `maxPOutliers = 0.1` caps
how many count as outliers, as the FAQ suggests. The soft power raises correlations to make the
network approximately scale-free; `pickSoftThreshold()` returns the lowest power whose fit reaches
R² 0.85, and the FAQ's table value for a signed network on more than 40 samples, 12, stands in if
none does.

```{r soft-threshold}
#| results: hide
soft <- pickSoftThreshold(
  expression,
  powerVector = c(1:10, seq(12, 20, 2)), networkType = "signed", corFnc = "bicor",
  corOptions = list(maxPOutliers = 0.1), verbose = 0
)
power <- coalesce(soft$powerEstimate, 12)
soft_threshold <- transmute(
  soft$fitIndices,
  power = Power, signed_r2 = -sign(slope) * SFT.R.sq, mean_connectivity = mean.k.
)
```

```{r power}
power
```

## Find modules

`blockwiseModules()` builds the network in one block and cuts the topological-overlap tree into
modules with the tutorial settings: at least 30 proteins, modules merged when their eigengenes
correlate above 0.75 (`mergeCutHeight = 0.25`). Module 0 (grey) holds the proteins no module
takes, and it is never tested.

```{r modules}
network <- blockwiseModules(
  expression,
  power = power, networkType = "signed", TOMType = "signed", corType = "bicor",
  maxPOutliers = 0.1, minModuleSize = 30, mergeCutHeight = 0.25, deepSplit = 2,
  pamRespectsDendro = FALSE, maxBlockSize = 5000, numericLabels = TRUE, verbose = 0
)
modules <- paste0("M", network$colors)
eigengenes <- network$MEs |>
  select(-ME0) |>
  rename_with(function(x) sub("ME", "M", x)) |>
  t()
```

Module membership (kME) is each protein's bicor with each eigengene; a protein's kME with its own
module says how central it is.

```{r membership}
kme <- signedKME(
  expression, network$MEs, corFnc = "bicor", corOptions = "maxPOutliers = 0.1"
)
membership <- tibble(
  protein = colnames(expression), gene = proteins$genes$Genes, module = modules,
  kme = kme[cbind(seq_len(nrow(kme)), match(paste0("kME", network$colors), colnames(kme)))]
) |>
  arrange(module, desc(kme))
count(membership, module)
```

## Test the eigengenes

Eigengenes carry no standard errors, so they go through plain limma, with the stage 02 design
(participant fixed) and its five contrasts. With about ten rows there is little for `eBayes()` to
borrow, so, as for log2 MPE in `05_Mitochondria/02_test_mito`, the test is the least-squares t with
`df.residual` degrees of freedom and a 95% interval. BH runs within each contrast across modules.
`plain_t()` turns one coefficient of a fit into that table.

```{r plain-t}
plain_t <- function(fit, coef) {
  tibble(
    module = rownames(fit$coefficients), estimate = fit$coefficients[, coef],
    se = fit$stdev.unscaled[, coef] * fit$sigma, df = fit$df.residual
  ) |>
    mutate(
      t = estimate / se, p = 2 * pt(-abs(t), df),
      conf.low = estimate - qt(0.975, df) * se, conf.high = estimate + qt(0.975, df) * se,
      fdr = p.adjust(p, "BH")
    )
}
```

```{r contrast-tests}
contrast_fit <- contrasts.fit(lmFit(eigengenes, d$design), d$contrasts)
eigengene_tests <- map(set_names(colnames(d$contrasts)), function(cn) plain_t(contrast_fit, cn)) |>
  list_rbind(names_to = "contrast")
filter(eigengene_tests, fdr < 0.05)
```

The association slope uses the eight designs of `03_Protein_Association`: each module's eigengene
change against each leg's outcome change, pooled over legs and within participant, coefficient
`post:x`. BH runs within each analysis and outcome across modules.

```{r association-tests}
eigengene_association <- imap(association_designs, function(design, ranking) {
  plain_t(lmFit(eigengenes, design), "post:x")
}) |>
  list_rbind(names_to = "ranking") |>
  separate_wider_delim(ranking, "_", names = c("analysis", "outcome"), too_many = "merge")
filter(eigengene_association, fdr < 0.05)
```

## Enrich the modules

`fgsea::fora()` runs a hypergeometric test of each module's genes against the project's one set
list, with every measured gene as the universe and the size limits of `01_run_fgsea_and_fry`; its
`padj` is BH within the module.

```{r enrichment}
module_genes <- membership |>
  filter(module != "M0", protein %in% gene_of$protein) |>
  mutate(gene = gene_of$gene[match(protein, gene_of$protein)])
enrichment <- map(split(module_genes$gene, module_genes$module), function(genes) {
  fgsea::fora(sets, genes, universe = gene_of$gene, minSize = 15, maxSize = 500)
}) |>
  list_rbind(names_to = "module") |>
  mutate(overlapGenes = map_chr(overlapGenes, paste, collapse = ";"))
enrichment |>
  filter(padj < 0.05) |>
  slice_min(padj, n = 3, by = module) |>
  select(module, pathway, overlap, padj)
```

## Check preservation

Module preservation (Langfelder et al. 2011, doi:10.1371/journal.pcbi.1001057) asks whether the
modules found in the pre-training samples hold in the post-training ones. Zsummary above 10 is
strong evidence of preservation, 2 to 10 weak to moderate, below 2 none. The module labels come
from all samples, so this check is mildly optimistic. 200 permutations, seeded.

```{r preservation}
pre <- targets$timepoint == "T1"
preserved <- modulePreservation(
  list(T1 = list(data = expression[pre, ]), T2 = list(data = expression[!pre, ])),
  list(T1 = labels2colors(network$colors)),
  referenceNetworks = 1, nPermutations = 200, networkType = "signed", corFnc = "bicor",
  corOptions = "maxPOutliers = 0.1", randomSeed = 1, savePermutedStatistics = FALSE, verbose = 0
)
z <- preserved$preservation$Z$ref.T1$inColumnsAlsoPresentIn.T2
ranks <- preserved$preservation$observed$ref.T1$inColumnsAlsoPresentIn.T2
colour_of <- set_names(paste0("M", network$colors), labels2colors(network$colors))
preservation <- tibble(
  module = colour_of[rownames(z)], colour = rownames(z), size = z$moduleSize,
  z_summary = z$Zsummary.pres, median_rank = ranks[rownames(z), "medianRank.pres"]
) |>
  filter(!colour %in% c("grey", "gold")) |>
  arrange(desc(z_summary))
preservation
```

## Draw figures

One A4 PDF: the soft-threshold fit, the protein dendrogram with module colours (WGCNA's own
`plotDendroAndColors()`), and a heatmap of module t statistics across the contrasts and the
association slopes, labelled where BH-adjusted p < 0.05.

```{r figures}
threshold_page <- ggplot(soft_threshold, aes(power, signed_r2, label = power)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.85, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey60") +
  geom_text(size = 3) +
  annotate("point", x = power, y = soft_threshold$signed_r2[soft_threshold$power == power],
    shape = 21, size = 6, colour = "#B2182B"
  ) +
  labs(x = "soft power", y = "scale-free fit, signed R²", title = "Soft-threshold choice") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10)
heatmap_rows <- bind_rows(
  transmute(eigengene_tests, module, column = contrast, t, fdr),
  transmute(eigengene_association, module, column = paste(analysis, outcome), t, fdr)
) |>
  mutate(
    column = factor(column, unique(column)),
    module = factor(module, rev(paste0("M", sort(unique(network$colors[network$colors > 0])))))
  )
heatmap_page <- ggplot(heatmap_rows, aes(column, module, fill = t)) +
  geom_tile(colour = "white") +
  geom_text(aes(label = if_else(fdr < 0.05, sprintf("%.2g", fdr), "")), size = 2.5) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#2166AC", mid = "white", high = "#B2182B", name = "t") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, title = "Module eigengenes: contrasts and association slopes") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 9) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1), panel.grid = element_blank())
pdf(file.path(stage, "b_reports", "01_modules.pdf"), width = 8.27, height = 11.69)
print(threshold_page)
plotDendroAndColors(
  network$dendrograms[[1]], labels2colors(network$colors[network$blockGenes[[1]]]),
  "module", dendroLabels = FALSE, hang = 0.03, main = "Protein dendrogram and modules"
)
print(heatmap_page)
invisible(dev.off())
```

## Save results

`01_modules.xlsx` holds one sheet per table.

```{r write}
write_xlsx(
  list(
    soft_threshold = soft_threshold, membership = membership,
    eigengene_tests = eigengene_tests, eigengene_association = eigengene_association,
    enrichment = arrange(enrichment, module, padj), preservation = preservation
  ),
  file.path(stage, "c_data", "01_modules.xlsx")
)
```
